# Story 06 — System Configuration & Branding

---

## Prerequisites

- Story 02 — Users Management completed (admin user identity and JWT bearer flow available).
- Story 03 — Roles & Permissions completed. New permission keys will be added to `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Roles/Permissions.cs` and wired into the `[HasPermission]` policy pipeline used by other admin controllers.
- Optional but recommended: skim Story 04 — Departments & Branches and Story 05 — Audit Logs for the CRUD controller/service pattern this story follows.
- Coordinate with the owner of `frontend/src/components/AppLayout.tsx` — branding fields (app name, logo, primary color) will be consumed there.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver a **single-tenant** system configuration + branding surface for the Customer Support CRM:

1. Authorized administrators can view the current system configuration and branding settings.
2. Authorized administrators can update the supported system configuration settings (application name, support email, default timezone, default culture).
3. Authorized administrators can configure branding (application display name, logo URL, primary color, secondary color).
4. Branding is reflected in the running CRM interface (topbar/AppLayout title, favicon-adjacent logo, primary theme color).
5. Unauthorized callers receive HTTP 403 from write endpoints and never see the settings admin UI.

**Not in scope:** multi-tenant configuration, feature flags, email templates, i18n toggles, uploading logo binaries (URL only), audit-log wiring for setting changes (may be added later, out of scope here).

## Product rules (from story)

- The CRM is single-tenant: exactly **one** system-settings row exists. GET returns it; PUT upserts it. There is no create/delete endpoint.
- Supported configuration fields (initial set, minimal):
  - `applicationName` (string, required, ≤ 120)
  - `supportEmail` (string, required, valid email, ≤ 200)
  - `defaultTimezone` (IANA id string, required, ≤ 100, default `UTC`)
  - `defaultCulture` (string, required, ≤ 20, default `en-US`)
- Supported branding fields:
  - `brandDisplayName` (string, required, ≤ 120) — falls back to `applicationName` on the UI when blank.
  - `logoUrl` (string, optional, ≤ 500, must be absolute `http(s)://…` when present)
  - `primaryColor` (string, required, `#RRGGBB` hex)
  - `secondaryColor` (string, required, `#RRGGBB` hex)
- Only administrators with the new permissions may read or write settings. Unauthorized callers receive `403 Forbidden`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Anonymous request to `GET /api/system-settings`** → 401 from `[Authorize]`. Enforced in `SystemSettingsController`.
- **Authenticated user without `system-settings.read`** → 403 from `PermissionAuthorizationHandler` (`backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Authorization/PermissionAuthorizationHandler.cs`).
- **PUT with invalid hex color** → 400 with validation message. Enforced in `SystemSettingsService.UpdateAsync`.
- **PUT with relative or non-http(s) `LogoUrl`** → 400. Same location.
- **Empty database / missing row** → service performs read-or-create on `Id = 1` so first PUT after a rollback still works.
- **Concurrent PUTs** → last-write-wins; document by comment in service. No optimistic concurrency token required for this story.
- **Frontend load fails (network / 403 for non-admin viewer)** → `BrandingContext` swallows error and uses defaults; do **not** block the app from rendering.
- **`logoUrl` present but 404 at runtime** → `<img onError>` in `AppLayout` hides the broken image; UI falls back to text.
- **Very long `applicationName`/`brandDisplayName`** → truncated by MUI with CSS ellipsis in the header; server enforces max length.
- **`primaryColor` equals `secondaryColor`** → allowed; no rule against it.

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration name: `AddSystemSettings`. Adds one table (`SystemSettings`) with the fields listed in step 3.
- Seeder is idempotent (`if (!db.SystemSettings.Any())`).
- Rollback: `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigrationName>` from `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api` drops the `SystemSettings` table.
- Half-applied risk: if the migration ran but the seeder did not, `GET` will 500 until PUT creates the row — service handles this by treating missing row as defaults on GET and upserting on PUT.
